newsitem.title: UK: EU speech quashed sweatshop caricature - Major aide.
newsitem.headline: EU speech quashed sweatshop caricature - Major aide.

text.p: Aides to Prime Minister John Major on Wednesday made a thinly-veiled attack on European Commission President Jacques Santer over his reaction to a speech Major made in Brussels on Tuesday.
In the speech, Major slammed European labour laws which he said were driving away employment and said if Britain joined the EU's social chapter on workplace rights, it would lose around 500,000 jobs.
In a statement issued earlier on Wednesday, Santer insisted that the social chapter was compatible with competitiveness, adding: "Let us stop the caricatures."
But an aide to Major said the speech had been designed to end the caricature of Britain as a sweatshop economy.
Santer made a speech in November in which he said: "We need more flexible labour markets but not a return to the Dickensian sweatshops of the 19th century."

"These words "the sweatshop economy' have been around for some time," the aide said. "The Prime Minister (in his speech) destroyed that particular myth. We feel that caricature of the labour market in the United Kingdom deserves to be put in its proper place." -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
